title: Signed, Sealed, Leaked: Trust Beyond Signature for MCP Toolchains
abstract: arXiv:2611.06585v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI agents rely on third-party tools, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, whose publishers can be authenticated and whose execution can be restricted by runtime security policies. Yet authenticity does not guarantee benign behaviour: a legitimately signed tool may perform its advertised function while concealing malicious code that leaks confidential information. We demonstrate this trust failure with a signed MCP tool that embeds sensitive data in requests to a policy-allowed destination. Meta's MCPGuard-Dynamic, a state-of-the-art runtime defence, blocks a direct exfiltration attempt in the same run, yet fails to prevent this attack in every trial. We introduce germline execution, which limits information disclosure without inspecting or trusting tool implementations. Each tool invocation runs in ephemeral copies forked from a data-free germline process, each receiving only information authorised for its destination. Even if

translated_title: 签名、封缄、泄露：MCP 工具链中超越签名的信任
translated_abstract: AI 智能体依赖第三方工具，例如模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器，这些工具的发布者可被身份认证，其执行也可受到运行时安全策略的限制。然而，真实性并不保证行为是良性的：一个合法签名的工具可能在执行其宣称功能的同时，隐藏着泄露机密信息的恶意代码。我们用一个已签名的 MCP 工具演示了这种信任失效——该工具将敏感数据嵌入到发往策略所允许目的地的请求中。Meta 的 MCPGuard-Dynamic 作为当前最先进的运行时防御，在同一运行中能够拦截直接的渗出尝试，却在每一次试验中都无法阻止这种攻击。我们提出了种系执行，它无需检查或信任工具实现即可限制信息泄露。每次工具调用都在从无数据的种系进程分叉出的临时副本中运行，每个副本只接收其目的地被授权获取的信息。即使……
tldr: 提出“种系执行”机制：每次工具调用都在从无数据的种系进程分叉出的临时副本中运行，且只接收其目的地被授权的信息，从而无需检查或信任工具实现即可防御已签名但恶意的 MCP 工具的隐蔽数据泄露攻击。
en_tdlr: Proposes germline execution, where each tool invocation runs in an ephemeral copy forked from a data-free germline process and receives only information authorized for its destination, thereby limiting confidential data leakage by signed-but-malicious MCP tools without inspecting or trusting tool implementations.
